name: Tannheimer Tal
kurzbeschreibung: High-altitude valley in the Allgäuer Alpen – famous for its Vilsalpsee mountain backdrop, kilometers of hiking trails, and traditional alpine farming.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Tannheimer Tal unfolds as an enchanting, sun-drenched high-alpine valley at an elevation of roughly 1,100 meters in northwestern Tyrol, directly adjoining the Bavarian Allgäu. Repeatedly voted "Europe's most beautiful high valley" by travel publications, this 16-kilometer-long alpine plateau harmonizes wide, pastoral meadows, deep-rooted rural traditions, and jagged limestone sentinels. Cradled by legendary hiking and climbing massifs—such as the formidable Rote Flüh (2,108 m), the Gimpel spire, and the panoramic Neunerköpfle—the valley provides an awe-inspiring alpine amphitheater. Anchored by the turquoise Vilsalpsee nature reserve and the inviting bathing waters of Lake Haldensee, the valley forms a paradise for casual walkers, water sports fans, and mountaineers alike.

Route & Requirements

Trail diversity in the Tannheimer Tal spans gentle valley strolls to severe vertical rock climbing. Families adore the level circular promenade around Lake Haldensee (4.5 km, 1.5 hours, easy grade T1, completely barrier-free and stroller accessible) or the pastoral walk into the Vilsalpsee nature reserve. Modern cable cars provide effortless access to high elevations: the 8-seater Neunerköpfle gondola leads to the interactive "9erlebnisweg" sensory trail and the famous "World's Largest Summit Book" at over 1,860 meters (easy family ridge walk T1). Seasoned mountaineers tackle the challenging Lachenspitze Via Ferrata (grade C/D) or rock scrambles up the Rote Flüh (alpine grade T3/T4). Furthermore, the valley is celebrated as an international road cycling and gravel hub featuring over 2,500 km of interconnected routes. Comfortable footwear suffices on valley paths, while rigid hiking boots are essential on ridges. Leashed dogs are warmly welcomed on all valley and alpine trails.

Visit & Arrival

By rail, travelers arrive via Reutte in Tirol station or Sonthofen station in Bavaria. Connecting regional VVT bus lines 120 and 121 run frequently throughout the valley, serving all villages from Nesselwängle through Tannheim to Schattwald. Motorists arriving from Germany enjoy toll- and vignette-free access via autobahn A7 (exit Oy-Mittelberg) across the scenic Oberjoch Pass. From Austria, access leads via Reutte over the Weißenbach Pass. Ample parking is situated at all lift bases and trailheads.

Tips

Book a stay with partner hosts offering "Summer Cable Cars Included," granting complimentary daily rides on mountain lifts in Tannheim, Grän, Nesselwängle, and Schattwald, as well as free admission to Haldensee outdoor swimming lido. Savor handcrafted alpine mountain cheese and fresh sourdough bread on the sun deck of Vilsalpe or Krinnenalpe.

saison: Ganzjährig zugänglich (Sommersaison Mai bis Oktober ideal)
